2610.12376.title: Latent Core Tokenizer: Compress, but Meaningfully
2610.12376.paper_summary: Tokenizers are commonly optimized for compression, but a compact vocabulary does not necessarily distribute its capacity evenly across languages. We introduce the Latent Core Tokenizer (LCT), a language-agnostic approach that separates structural discovery from vocabulary construction. LCT uses Minimum Description Length, entropy-based boundary signals, and morphotactic constraints to identify reusable linguistic units before constructing a shared vocabulary. Across 104 languages with a 200K-token vocabulary, LCT achieves lower fertility and higher MorphScore than BPE, Unigram, and parity-aware BPE, while maintaining comparable cross-lingual disparity in tokenization cost. Across four multilingual downstream benchmarks, LCT improves aggregate score by 1.48, 1.83, and 2.00 points over BPE, Unigram, and parity-aware BPE, respectively. Our findings show that compression alone does not predict representation quality and highlight the importance of morphology-driven structural discovery and how frequency is used to allocate the final vocabulary across languages.
2610.12376.paper_summary_zh: Tokenizers 通常是針對壓縮進行優化的，但緊湊的詞彙表並不一定在各種語言之間均勻分配其容量。<lb/>我們介紹了潛在核心分詞器（Latent Core Tokenizer, LCT），這是一種與語言無關的方法，將結構發現與詞彙構建分開。<lb/>LCT 使用最小描述長度、基於熵的邊界信號和形態約束來識別可重用的語言單元，然後再構建共享的詞彙表。<lb/>在 104 種語言中，使用 200K-token 的詞彙表，LCT 在生育率上表現得比 BPE、Unigram 和考慮平衡的 BPE 更低，並且在 MorphScore 上更高，同時在分詞成本的跨語言差異上保持可比性。<lb/>在四個多語言的下游基準測試中，LCT 分別比 BPE、Unigram 和考慮平衡的 BPE 提高了 1.48、1.83 和 2.00 分的總分。<lb/>我們的研究結果顯示，僅僅依賴壓縮無法預測表示質量，並強調了形態驅動的結構發現的重要性，以及如何使用頻率來在各種語言之間分配最終的詞彙表。
